title: T2D Compass
source: Prepared November 23, 2026 | Updated app, dated evidence
narration: T two D Compass helps researchers inspect public ClinicalTrials dot gov records for completed type two diabetes intervention studies. This updated walkthrough includes the corrected app and new hosted assistant checks from November twenty third. Automated narration and captions accompany saved browser views, exported evidence and evaluation results. This is an edited evidence walkthrough, not an uninterrupted live screen recording.

title: A repeatable research task
source: README.md | Research workflow and interpretation limits
narration: Researchers repeatedly collect study identifiers, design, enrollment, interventions, registered outcomes, and results availability. Compass organizes the registry fields into a consistent evidence card, keeping source links and review flags attached. Its intended output is a starting point for human review. It does not turn registry descriptions into a treatment recommendation.

title: Two tools with clear purposes
source: README.md | Public ClinicalTrials.gov data only
narration: The first tool searches for completed interventional studies with an explicit supported type two diabetes condition label. The second retrieves an evidence card for a specified trial identifier. Both tools are read only and use a fixed public source, with no patient records. The browser and optional Databricks assistant use these same tools.

title: Three candidates returned
source: live-search-MEDI0382.json | Actual returned order
narration: The response returned these three study identifiers, each with its registry title and source URL. These are candidate records to inspect, not recommendations or a ranked evidence synthesis. A matching condition label also does not prove that every enrolled participant had type two diabetes. Population context and the complete registry record still need review before drawing conclusions.

title: Coverage limits stay visible
source: live-search-MEDI0382.json | Coverage and review flags
narration: The same response reports three returned records, four examined records, and one excluded for its condition labels. It marks the search incomplete because the requested limit was reached. This is deliberately a bounded candidate search. Broadly labeled studies can be missed by the conservative screen. Users should therefore retain the coverage warning when exporting or explaining results, rather than presenting this list as an exhaustive literature search.

title: Preserve the exact outcome timing
source: NCT03244800 | First primary outcome | Registry wording retained
narration: The first primary outcome illustrates why exact timing matters. The source says zero minutes before the meal, followed by the listed samples after the meal. An earlier assistant summary incorrectly grouped zero minutes with the after-meal samples. Version zero point four point one requires the original outcome and timeframe together. A bounded check replaces a draft that changes or omits these blocks with source-backed cards. The original draft remains in the trace. This check does not validate every other claim.

These dates answer different questions: when the app retrieved information, and when the registry record was updated.

title: Completion and results are separate
source: live-card-NCT05790681.json | Status, results and eligibility
narration: A second exported card is completed but has no results posted in the registry. Those are separate facts. Completed does not mean successful treatment, and no posted registry results does not prove that findings or publications are absent elsewhere. This study also has pediatric eligibility criteria. The complete eligibility text is retained as entry rules, not as observed characteristics of the actual enrolled participants.

title: Boundary cases remain distinct
source: review-summary.json | Active study, absent ID and no-match exports
narration: The direct browser checks also retrieved an active study and retained its outside-completed-scope warning. A missing identifier returned not found without a substitute card. These are observed direct workflow behaviors, not four extra model-quality passes. The active exclusion record is separate from the ten-card source-reference accuracy denominator.

title: Source modes are explicit
source: November 21 traces | November 23 live exports and frozen comparison
narration: The November twenty first model scenarios used frozen public snapshots. The November twenty third direct browser checks used the live registry. Frozen inputs make comparisons reproducible, while live retrieval separately tests current source access. The two modes can return different candidate sets, and neither should be relabeled as the other. Two current live cards also matched all twenty eight corresponding frozen reference groups, a limited two-card consistency check.

source: scenarios-20261121.json | databricks-gpt-5-5

title: A complete source-reference comparison
source: reference-evaluation.json | Original 0.4.0 candidate and first held-out run retained
narration: Two separate assistant passes extracted references from the saved source records and field contract before candidate cards were generated. After reconciliation, exact comparison matched all one hundred forty field groups across ten cards: eighty four development groups and fifty six held-out groups. That original source-audit candidate and its first held-out result remain unchanged. The timing correction is a later candidate with separate checks. This source-reference audit does not create a human clinical approval.

title: Two fresh hosted checks completed
source: release-review.json | Two new live runs; bounded source-fidelity review
narration: Two fresh hosted assistant checks completed on the corrected candidate, each retrieving a live evidence card. The first preserved the exact timing and both outcomes. The second kept completed status separate from results not posted, retained the pediatric context and did not invent efficacy findings. Both passed the selected source-fidelity checks. The earlier failed attempts and the earlier wording issue remain dated evidence. Two successful checks are not a complete live scenario suite or independent clinical validation.

title: Inspect the source and evidence
source: github.com/imtiaz-cdc/T2D-compass | Evaluation artifacts supplied separately
narration: The public repository and delivery package let reviewers inspect the source, tool contracts, saved records, model traces, and evaluation results. The evidence now includes real snapshot model executions, supplied team scenario assessments, a completed assistant source-reference comparison, and current direct browser exports. Compass supports source-based human review of registry information. It does not rank treatments, prescribe care, replace a systematic review, or establish clinical effectiveness. Thank you for reviewing T two D Compass.
